data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's claim that independence is unfalsifiable overgeneralizes from extreme-value statistics to a universal. The mechanism only shows that for a FINITE observation window there always exists a rare shared cause below detection threshold; it does not establish that every shared cause is unobservable in principle. The problem explicitly asks to 'identify what evidence would distinguish' the two failure-mode classes, and SRC_002's own first countercondition (complete advance enumeration of shared causes, with none shared by decentralized operators) is exactly such distinguishing evidence — and is not shown to be impossible. If operators can be proven to draw from disjoint dependency sets (distinct power grids, distinct codebases, distinct supply chains), then 'a shared cause will always be found post hoc' is false: an enumerated-complete shared-cause set with zero intersection leaves no latent common cause to be discovered. By asserting unfalsifiability while listing a countercondition that defeats it, SRC_002 contradicts itself rather than defending the claim, so the argument fails to hold even on its own terms.
